Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas of support that might be helpful to you during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us a sense of how you've been feeling over the past week.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. My goal is to provide you with a non-judgmental and empathetic ear, and to work together to identify any resources or support that might be beneficial to you.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and we'll take them one at a time. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Don't worry about "right" or "wrong" answers – I just want to understand your perspective and experiences.

Let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things that usually bring you happiness?

(nervously) Oh, thank you for having me... I'm not really sure where to start. I mean, I've been feeling pretty overwhelmed with the baby and everything. It's just been a lot to take in, you know? (pauses) As for enjoying things, I'd say it's been a bit of a struggle. I used to love reading and taking long walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or motivation to do those things. I mean, I'm exhausted all the time from caring for the baby, and when I do get some free time, I just end up sleeping or worrying about the baby's health. (sighs) It's like, I love my baby, but I just feel so... tired and anxious all the time. (looks down) I do get some pleasure from spending time with my baby, though. Like, when she smiles at me or something, it's just... (smiles slightly) it's the best feeling in the world. But overall, I'd say I've been feeling a bit down and unsure of myself as a mom. (pauses, looking for reassurance) Does that sound... normal?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(slightly smiling) Yeah, I'd say that's been a bit of a challenge for me lately. I mean, I do laugh and find things funny, but it's not as often as it used to be. Most of the time, I'm just so worried about the baby and whether I'm doing everything right... (trails off) I don't know, it's just hard to find the humor in things when you're running on fumes and feeling anxious all the time. (pauses) But, like I said, when my baby does something cute or funny, it can still make me laugh. It's just... it's not as easy to laugh and find the funny side of things like it used to be. (looks down, slightly concerned) I feel like I've lost a bit of myself, you know? Like, I'm just "mom" now, and not really... me. (sighs) Does that make sense?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head slightly) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll think about things I want to do, like taking a shower without interruptions or going for a walk, but then I just feel too tired or overwhelmed to actually do them. (sighs) And when I do try to plan something, I just get anxious about how it will affect the baby or whether I'll be able to get everything done. It's hard to enjoy looking forward to things when you're just trying to get through the day. (pauses) But, like I said, there are moments with my baby that I really look forward to, like when my husband comes home from work and we get to spend time together as a family. Those moments are really special to me. (smiles slightly) But overall, it's just been hard to find the energy and motivation to look forward to things like I used to. Everything just feels so... daunting right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding slightly) Yeah, that's happened a few times. I'll be taking care of the baby and something will go wrong, like she'll spit up all over her clothes, and I'll just feel like it's all my fault. Like, I should have been able to prevent it or something. (sighs) And then I'll start thinking about all the things I could have done differently, and it just spirals into this cycle of self-blame and guilt. (looks down) It's hard to shake the feeling that I'm not doing enough or that I'm not good enough as a mom. (pauses) But, I mean, my husband is always telling me that I'm doing a great job and that it's okay to make mistakes. He's really supportive, and that helps. (smiles slightly) It's just... sometimes it's hard to see things from a rational perspective when you're in the midst of it all. (trails off) I guess I just wish I could be kinder to myself and not beat myself up over every little thing.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding more emphatically) Oh, yeah. That's been a big one for me. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? Or what if she's not developing like she's supposed to? (bites lip) Or even just things like, what if I'm not making enough milk? Or what if I'm doing something wrong and it's going to hurt her? (shakes head) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that's always there, lurking in the back of my mind. (sighs) And it's not even like I can pinpoint what's causing it, you know? It's just this general sense of unease and worry. (pauses) Sometimes I'll be up at night, feeding the baby, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios. (looks up, eyes wide) It's exhausting, to be honest. I just wish I could turn it off, you know? Just be able to relax and enjoy this time with my baby without all these worries and fears.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to... I don't know, like I'm going to lose control or something. (shakes head) It's really scary, because it feels like it comes out of nowhere. I'll be thinking about something, like the baby's schedule or what I need to do that day, and then suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear. (pauses) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to something, even though my mind knows that everything is okay. (looks down) I've had a few times where I've been holding the baby, and I'll just feel this panic rise up, and I'll think, "What if I drop her?" or "What if something happens to her?" (shakes head again) It's just this irrational fear that takes over, and it's really hard to calm myself down. (takes another deep breath) But, like I said, it's not all the time. It's just... sometimes. (trails off, looking concerned)
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding) Yeah, that's definitely been true lately. I mean, taking care of a newborn is just so all-consuming, you know? It's like, every moment of every day is dedicated to this tiny human, and it's exhausting. (sighs) I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water most of the time. Between feeding and changing and soothing, and trying to get some sleep... it's just a lot. (looks down) And on top of that, I'm trying to recover from the birth, and my hormones are all over the place... it's just a lot to deal with. (pauses) Some days, I feel like I'm managing okay, but other days, it just feels like everything is too much. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm going to lose it. (laughs slightly) I mean, it's not like I'm expecting to have it all together or anything, but... (trails off) I guess I just feel like I'm not doing a very good job of keeping everything under control. (looks up, seeking reassurance) Does that make sense?
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yeah, that's been a problem for me too. I mean, I'm already not sleeping much because the baby wakes up a lot at night, but even when I do get a chance to sleep, I often find myself lying awake, worrying about things or just feeling really down. (sighs) It's like, my mind is racing and I just can't seem to turn it off. (pauses) And then, when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these awful dreams or I'll wake up feeling really anxious, and it's just... it's hard to shake off. (looks down) I've had a few nights where I've just lain there, feeling so overwhelmed and unhappy, and I just didn't know how I was going to get through the next day. (pauses again) But, I mean, it's not every night. Some nights are better than others. (shrugs slightly) I guess it just depends on how I'm feeling, you know? (looks up) But, yeah, sleep has been a real challenge for me lately. (yawns slightly, showing fatigue) Sorry, I'm just really tired, I guess.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding slowly) Yeah... I'd say that's been true for me, too. I mean, I've had moments where I've just felt really down, you know? Like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. (pauses, getting choked up) Or, I'll be thinking about how hard everything is, and how I'm not doing a good enough job, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. (wipes away a tear) It's like, I'm happy to have my baby, and I love her so much, but at the same time, I just feel so... overwhelmed and sad. (sighs) And it's not just about the baby, it's about me, too. I feel like I've lost myself, you know? Like, I'm just a mom now, and I don't know who I am anymore. (looks down, voice cracking) It's just really hard, and it feels like nobody understands what I'm going through. (pauses, taking a deep breath) But, I mean, it's not all the time. Some days are better than others. (smiles slightly) And when my baby smiles at me, or when my husband is being really supportive, it makes me feel a little better. (looks up) But, yeah, the sadness is definitely there, and it's something I'm struggling with.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in her eyes) Yeah... I've been crying a lot lately. (pauses to collect herself) It's just that everything feels so overwhelming, and I'm so tired, and I just feel like I'm not doing anything right. (wipes away a tear) I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and just suddenly I'll start crying. (sighs) It's like, I'll be fine one minute, and then the next minute I'll just be sobbing. (looks down, embarrassed) It's hard to explain, but it's just like all these emotions are bottled up inside me, and then they just come pouring out. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I've cried in front of my husband, and he's always trying to comfort me, but it's just... (shrugs) I don't know, it's just really hard to stop once I start. (looks up, tears streaming down her face) I feel like I'm just so emotional all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. (sobs slightly) I just feel like I'm a mess, and I don't know how to be a good mom when I'm feeling like this.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking her head firmly) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, but I've never thought about harming myself. (pauses, looking relieved) I'm just really struggling to cope with everything, but I don't feel like I'm in danger of hurting myself. (looks up, seeking reassurance) I'm just glad to be talking to you about all this, because it feels like a weight is being lifted off my shoulders. (smiles slightly) I feel like I can finally be honest about how I'm feeling, and that's a really big relief. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I just want to be a good mom, and I want to be happy, and I feel like I'm taking steps in the right direction just by talking about all this. (looks down, smiling slightly) So, no, I don't have any thoughts of harming myself. I just need some help and support to get through this tough time.

The patient, a new mother, is experiencing a range of emotional and psychological challenges, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, as well as anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed. She reports difficulty sleeping, with mood-related sleep disturbances, and feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-blame, particularly related to her role as a mother. The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with postpartum depression and anxiety, and she requires further evaluation and support to ensure her emotional well-being and ability to care for her newborn.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 20, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Definitely not so much now' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have looked forward with enjoyment to things 'definitely less' than before, as they express feeling too tired or overwhelmed to do things they want to do and struggle to find energy and motivation.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to blaming themselves unnecessarily when things go wrong, specifically mentioning it happens when taking care of the baby and things don't go as planned, indicating it occurs 'some of the time</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a constant and nagging feeling of anxiety that is always present, with worries and fears arising frequently, even at night, and affecting their ability to enjoy time with their baby.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes experiencing panic and fear for no apparent reason, but also mentions it doesn't happen all the time, which aligns with the 'Yes, sometimes' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they are having trouble coping with their new responsibilities as a mother, but also mentions that 'some days, I feel like I'm managing okay', which suggests that they are not completely unable to cope, but rather struggling at times.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports difficulty sleeping due to feeling unhappy, worrying, and having awful dreams, but also mentions that it's not every night and some nights are better than others, which aligns with the 'Yes, sometimes' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes feeling sad and overwhelmed, with moments of crying and feeling down for no reason, indicating that they experience sadness quite often, but also mentions that it's not all the time and some days are better than others.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports crying a lot lately, feeling overwhelmed, and having intense emotional outbursts, indicating that she has been unhappy and crying most of the time.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with postpartum depression and anxiety, as indicated by her EPDS score of 20. According to EPDS guidelines, a score of 12-13 indicates a high possibility of depression, and a score of 14 or higher indicates probable depression. The patient's symptoms, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, anxiety, panic, and feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-blame, are consistent with <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med> as defined in the <med>DSM-5</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices
3. Refer to <med>mental health specialist</med> for further evaluation and support
4. Provide patient with resources for postpartum depression and anxiety, such as support groups and online resources
5. Encourage patient to reach out to friends and family for emotional support
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

* Persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells
